 Belated Return Due Date for AY 2026-27: Check Deadline and Penalty
 Poojitha Raam Vinay 
 Poojitha Raam Vinay 
 Author 
 Follow 
 View profile 
 Last updated: 29 October 2026 
 Save 
 Share 
 Join Us 
 Follow Us 
 Add as Source 
 Every year, lakhs of taxpayers miss the 31 July deadline because of a pending Form 16, a corrected AIS, or plain procrastination. The good news is that the Income-tax Act gives you a second window. The bad news is that this window has a cost, and it closes for good on 31 December 2026.
 This guide explains the deadline, the exact penalty, what you lose by filing late, and what to do if even this date slips.
 Table Of Content
 What Is a Belated Return? 
 ITR Due Dates for AY 2026-27 at a Glance 
 Penalty for Belated Return: Section 234F Late Fee 
 Interest on Unpaid Tax: Sections 234A, 234B and 234C 
 What Else Do You Lose by Filing a Belated Return? 
 Can You Revise a Belated Return? 
 What If You Miss 31 December 2026 Too? 
 Step-by-Step: How to File a Belated Return 
 What Is a Belated Return?
 A belated return is an income tax return filed after the original due date under section 139(1) but within the extended period permitted by section 139(4). Although the Income-tax Act, 2025 has come into force from 1 April 2026, AY 2026-27 continues to be governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961, so the familiar sections 139(4), 234A and 234F apply.
 ITR Due Dates for AY 2026-27 at a Glance
 Taxpayer Category 
 Original Due Date 
 Last Date for Belated Return 
 Salaried individuals, HUFs and others not requiring audit (ITR-1, ITR-2) 
 31 July 2026 
 31 December 2026 
 Certain non-audit business and professional cases (ITR-3, ITR-4) 
 31 August 2026 
 31 December 2026 
 Audit cases, companies, working partners of audited firms 
 31 October 2026, extended to 21 November 2026 (CBDT Circular No. 07/2026 dated 28 September 2026) 
 31 December 2026 
 Transfer pricing cases 
 30 November 2026 
 31 December 2026 
 Note: The CBDT extension for audit cases moves only the original due date. The outer limit for a belated return stays at 31 December 2026 for everyone.
 Penalty for Belated Return: Section 234F Late Fee
 Section 234F is a flat fee for default in furnishing the return. It does not depend on how many days or months you are late. Filing one day late or five months late costs the same.
 Total Income 
 Late fee u/s 234F 
 Up to ₹5,00,000 
 ₹1,000 
 Above ₹5,00,000 
 ₹5,000 
 The fee applies even if your tax is fully covered by TDS and you owe nothing.
 It applies only if you were required to file. A person with no filing obligation who files voluntarily after the due date does not pay it.
 The portal calculates it automatically. It must be paid as self-assessment tax before you submit the return.
 Explore More in Details - Penalty For Late Filing Of Income Tax Return For AY 2026-27 
 Interest on Unpaid Tax: Sections 234A, 234B and 234C
 The late fee is the visible cost. Interest is the running cost.
 Section 234A: 1% per month or part of a month on tax still unpaid after TDS, TCS and advance tax, counted from the day after the due date until the date of filing.
 Section 234B: 1% per month if advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax.
 Section 234C: interest for deferment of advance tax instalments.
 Also Read - ITR Due Date Missed for AY 2026-27 
 What Else Do You Lose by Filing a Belated Return?
 The fee and interest are often the smaller problem. The bigger losses are these:
 Carry forward of losses: Business losses and capital losses of the year cannot be carried forward if the return is not filed by the due date. House property loss and unabsorbed depreciation can still be carried forward.
 Choice of tax regime: Individuals with business or professional income who miss the due date lose the option to opt out of the new tax regime for the year. Salaried taxpayers can still choose their regime while filing.
 Refund interest: Interest on refund under section 244A is paid only from the date you file, not from the start of the assessment year.
 Certain deductions and exemptions: Most Chapter VI-A deductions remain available in a belated return, but a few profit-linked deductions and exemptions require the return to be filed within the due date.
 Delayed processing and loan or visa paperwork: Refunds and ITR acknowledgements arrive later, which can affect loan approvals and visa applications.
 Prosecution risk: Wilful failure to file can attract prosecution under section 276CC in serious cases, so non-filing is never the safer option.
 Can You Revise a Belated Return?
 Yes. For AY 2026-27, a return filed under section 139(4) can be revised under section 139(5) up to 31 March 2027. Revisions made after 31 December 2026 attract a fee under the new section 234-I. Filing a correct belated return the first time still saves you time and cost.
 Explore in Details - Revised Return Due Date Extension 
 What If You Miss 31 December 2026 Too?
 After 31 December 2026, section 139(4) is no longer available. Your remaining option is an updated return (ITR-U) under section 139(8A), which can be filed within 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, but it costs more:
 When ITR-U is filed 
 Additional Tax on Tax and Interest Due 
 Within 12 months from end of AY 
 25% 
 12 to 24 months 
 50% 
 24 to 36 months 
 60% 
 36 to 48 months 
 70% 
 ITR-U generally cannot be used to claim a refund or to report a loss, so it is a poor substitute for filing on time.
 Step-by-Step: How to File a Belated Return
 Log in to the e-filing portal and pick AY 2026-27.
 Select the filing type as "Belated return u/s 139(4)".
 Choose the correct ITR form based on your income sources.
 Pre-fill from Form 26AS , AIS and TIS, and reconcile each entry with your documents.
 Compute tax, then pay the 234F fee and any 234A, 234B or 234C interest as self-assessment tax.
 Submit and e-verify within 30 days . An unverified return is treated as not filed.
 FAQs
 What is the last date to file a belated return for AY 2026-27? 
 31 December 2026, or before completion of assessment, whichever is earlier.
 What is the penalty for filing a belated return for AY 2026-27? 
 A late fee of ₹5,000 under section 234F (₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh), plus 1% per month interest under section 234A on unpaid tax.
 Can I file ITR after 31 December 2026? 
 Not as a belated return. You can file an updated return (ITR-U) under section 139(8A) with additional tax of 25% to 70%.
 Can a belated return be revised? 
 Yes, up to 31 March 2027, with a fee under section 234-I for revisions after 31 December 2026.
 Do I pay the 234F fee if I have no tax payable? 
 Yes, if you were required to file. It is a fee for default in filing, not interest on tax.
 Will I still get my refund if I file a belated return? 
 Yes. However, refund interest under section 244A runs only from the date of filing, and processing may take longer.
